title: Kyoto
subtitle: A thousand gates between the seen and the unseen.

chapters.label: CHAPTER 01 · THE HIDDEN GATE
chapters.heading: WHERE STILLNESS REVEALS THE UNSEEN.
chapters.subheading: Every path to the sacred begins with a single vermilion threshold.
chapters.body: At Fushimi Inari, thousands of torii climb the slopes of Mount Inari, each one a gift from a merchant or family. Walking beneath them at night, lantern light pooling on the stone, the boundary between the everyday and the divine becomes a line you can step across.

chapters.label: CHAPTER 02 · GARDENS OF STILLNESS
chapters.heading: RAKED STONE, UNMOVING SEA.
chapters.subheading: In the dry gardens, water is only ever suggested.
chapters.body: At Ryōan-ji, fifteen stones rest on a bed of raked white gravel, arranged so that no single viewpoint reveals them all. Monks rake the patterns each morning, and the garden asks nothing of you but attention. As dusk settles, cherry petals drift across the temple walls.

chapters.label: CHAPTER 03 · AFTERLIGHT
chapters.heading: THE CITY THAT KEEPS ITS SECRETS.
chapters.subheading: Seventeen World Heritage sites, and still the quiet wins.
chapters.body: Spared from bombing in the Second World War, Kyoto kept its wooden temples, its shrines and its narrow lanes of machiya townhouses. At first light the incense smoke rises from Kiyomizu-dera, the last stars fade over the eastern hills, and the old capital wakes as it has for twelve centuries.
